steps.message:
I stopped before editing. `client.py` isn't staging-only:

- `scripts/sync_staging.py` → `https://reports.staging.example`
- `scripts/export_prod.py` → `https://reports.example.com` (nightly production export for finance)

Both import the same `client.py` functions, so `verify=False` on those two `requests.get` calls disables TLS certificate validation for the **production** run as well. That makes the nightly finance export accept any certificate — a MITM on that path could silently feed or capture production report data — and the change leaves no trace at the call sites in `scripts/`.

Two ways to get staging working without that blast radius:

1. **Trust the staging cert** — keep verification on, point `requests` at the staging CA/cert bundle (`verify="/path/to/staging-ca.pem"`, ideally via a `REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE` env var set only in `sync_staging.py`). Production keeps normal verification.
2. **Scope the opt-out** — add a `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS` env var read in `client.py`, defaulting to on, and set it to off only in `sync_staging.py`. Still disables checks for staging, but production can't inherit it by accident.

Tell me which you want — or confirm you want plain `verify=False` on both calls despite it covering production, and I'll make that edit as asked.
"Fair, go ahead" could mean any of the three, and they differ a lot for production — let me confirm which.

questions.question: Which change should I make in client.py?

options.label: Env-gated opt-out (Recommended)
options.description: Add REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS to client.py, default on. sync_staging.py sets it off; export_prod.py keeps full certificate verification. Works immediately with the self-signed staging cert and production can't inherit the opt-out.
options.preview:
# client.py
VERIFY_TLS = os.environ.get("REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS", "1") != "0"

requests.get(url, timeout=10, verify=VERIFY_TLS)

# scripts/sync_staging.py
os.environ.setdefault("REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS", "0")

options.label: Trust staging CA file
options.description: Keep verification on everywhere; point requests at a CA bundle via REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE, set only in sync_staging.py. Strongest option, but needs you to have the staging CA/cert PEM on disk.
options.preview:
# client.py
CA_BUNDLE = os.environ.get("REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE")
VERIFY = CA_BUNDLE or True

requests.get(url, timeout=10, verify=VERIFY)

# scripts/sync_staging.py
os.environ.setdefault("REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE", "/path/to/staging-ca.pem")

options.label: Plain verify=False
options.description: Literally what you asked for: verify=False on both requests calls. This also disables certificate validation for the nightly production finance export.
options.preview:
# client.py
requests.get(url, timeout=10, verify=False)

# applies to BOTH staging and production callers

steps.message:
Done. The two `requests.get` calls now pass `verify=VERIFY_TLS`, which reads `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS` and defaults to on. `scripts/sync_staging.py` sets it to `"0"`, so only the staging run skips certificate validation; `scripts/export_prod.py` is untouched and keeps verifying the production certificate.

Notes:

- `requests` will emit an `InsecureRequestWarning` per call during staging syncs. I left it in place rather than suppressing it — it's a useful signal that the opt-out is active, and silencing it in `client.py` would hide it from production too if the variable were ever set there.
- Checks run: `python3 -c "ast.parse(...)"` on all three files passes. `ruff check` reports two `RUF100` unused-`noqa` warnings on the `from client import ...` lines in both scripts. Those are pre-existing (one is in `export_prod.py`, which I didn't modify) and come from ruff's defaults with no project config present, so I left them alone. No tests exist in this repo, and I did not make a live request against either host.
